title: In 1752, Britain went to bed on 2 September and woke on the 14th
body: To switch from the Julian to the Gregorian calendar, which Catholic Europe had used since 1582, Britain and its colonies dropped eleven days: Wednesday 2 September 1752 was followed by Thursday 14 September. Rent and contract dates were shifted so nobody gained or lost, which is why the UK tax year still ends on 5 April. Tales of mobs demanding ‘give us our eleven days’ are very likely a myth.

slides.question: When did Russia switch to the Gregorian calendar?
slides.explanation: 1918, and by then 13 days had to go (10 in 1582, 11 in 1752). The Bolsheviks switched soon after the revolution, so the ‘October’ Revolution of 1917 fell on 7 November, new style.

slides.question: What do historians make of the tales of mobs shouting ‘give us our eleven days’?
slides.explanation: Those tales are very likely a myth. Rent and contract dates were shifted so nobody gained or lost, which is why the UK tax year still ends on 5 April.

slides.heading: Which country did not switch in 1582?
slides.explanation: Spain, Portugal and France all adopted the Gregorian calendar in 1582, the year Pope Gregory XIII introduced it. Britain and its colonies held out until 1752.
